newsitem.title: USA: Pittsburgh agrees to settle police misconduct case.
newsitem.headline: Pittsburgh agrees to settle police misconduct case.

text.p: The Justice Department said Wednesday it had reached a settlement with the city of Pittsburgh after investigating allegations the police had engaged in a pattern of misconduct.
It said the agreement called for a number of steps, including the creation of guidelines for the city's police force in training, supervision, discipline and the handling of complaints.
The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division began investigating the police force's practices nearly a year ago after receiving complaints from citizens and community groups.
The complaints alleged excessive use of force and police misconduct in carrying out arrests and searches and seizures of evidence.

In October 1995, black motorist Jonny Gammage died as a result of a routine traffic stop by two white police officers near Pittsburgh. One officer stood on the back of his neck and pressed down with a metal club after, police alleged, Gammage had attacked them.
About 100 demonstrators from Pittsburgh came to the Justice Department last week to protest the incident.

According to the civil settlement filed in federal court in Pittsburgh, the city agreed to create an "early warning system" to identify potential problem officers and to alert managers to possible patterns of misconduct.

The city also agreed to require that police officers complete a report when force has been used, including during traffic stops, and to hire an independent auditor to monitor complaint investigations, the department said.
The civil agreement must be approved by a federal judge.
